001-252706.name: Kuijt v. the Netherlands
001-252706.subject: The case concerned an element of the practice of the Supreme Court of the Netherlands according to which, when a three- or five-judge panel of the relevant division – in the present case the Criminal Law Division- examines and decides on an appeal on points of law, other judges of the same division (called reservisten) may be present and participate in the discussion without taking part in the vote. The purpose of their participation is to ensure the uniform interpretation and application of the law as well as the consistency of the case-law of the Supreme Court.
conclusions: Article 6 § 1 – complaint that the applicant’s appeal on points of law was not determined by an independent “tribunal established by law”: inadmissible (non-exhaustion of domestic remedies)
Article 6 § 1 – complaint concerning the lack of judicial impartiality of the Supreme Court, on account of its reservisten system: inadmissible (manifestly ill-founded)

001-252214.name: Kavala v. Türkiye (no. 2)
001-252214.subject: The case concerned the measures taken against the applicant, in particular the criminal charges and proceedings against him, his conviction, sentence and detention, who considered them to have been imposed as a result of his activities and public stances as a human-rights defender. The case originated in the events following the Court’s judgment of 10 December 2019 (Kavala v. Turkey, no. 28749/18, 10 December 2019), after which the applicant continued to be deprived of his liberty before being sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment.
conclusions: Article 6 § 1 (fair hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal): violation
Article 6 § 1 (length of proceedings): inadmissible (non-exhaustion of domestic remedies)

001-251322.name: Jesus Pinhal v. Portugal
001-251322.subject: The case concerned three sets of proceedings brought against the applicant by the criminal-law authorities, the Securities Market Commission, and the Bank of Portugal, respectively, for various criminal and administrative offences committed when he was Vice-Chairman of the Board of Directors of a private bank.
conclusions: Article 4 of Protocol No. 7: no violation

001-251292.name: Grande Oriente d’Italia v. Italy
001-251292.subject: The case concerned the search of an Italian Masonic association’s premises ordered by a parliamentary commission of inquiry and the seizure of numerous paper and digital documents, including lists with the names and personal data of more than 6,000 of the association’s members. The search was ordered in the context of an investigation into the relationship between the Mafia and Freemasonry notably Mafia infiltration of masonic lodges in Calabria and Sicily and following the association’s rejection of the Commission’s requests to provide a list of its members.

001-251226.name: Vainik and Others v. Estonia
001-251226.subject: The case concerned the introduction of a total ban on smoking in prisons affecting the applicants, serving prisoners who were long-term smokers.
conclusions: Article 8: struck out of the list of cases (Article 37 § 1 (a) and (c) – death of one of the applicants during the Chamber proceedings and absence of intention on the part of the remaining two applicants to pursue their applications)

001-250157.name: Yasak v. Türkiye
001-250157.subject: The case concerned the applicant’s conviction for membership of an armed terrorist organisation referred to by the Turkish authorities as the “Fetullahist Terror Organisation/Parallel State Structure”, on the basis, inter alia, that he had been active at a level entailing responsibilities within the organisation and engaged in activities on its behalf. It also concerned the applicant’s conditions of detention in prison.

001-247839.name: Danileţ v. Romania
001-247839.subject: The case concerned a disciplinary sanction imposed on a judge by the National Judicial and Legal Service Commission for posting two messages on his Facebook page.

001-247738.name: Tsaava and Others v. Georgia
001-247738.subject: The case concerned the dispersal by the police of a demonstration in front of the Parliament building involving the firing of kinetic impact projectiles and physical force and resulting in injuries to the applicants (demonstrators and journalists). It also concerned the competence of the Court to refrain from deciding parts of an application before it.
conclusions: Article 34: competence of the Court to refrain from examining part of an individual application

001-245359.name: Kovačević v. Bosnia and Herzegovina
001-245359.subject: The case concerned the applicant’s inability to vote for candidates of his choice due to a combination of ethnic and territorial requirements governing the legislative and presidential elections at State level.
conclusions: Article 35 § 3 (a): abuse of the right of application)
Articles 34 and 35, Article 14 (+ Article 3 Protocol No. 1), Article 1 Protocol No. 12: lack of victim status

001-244348.name: Semenya v. Switzerland
001-244348.subject: The case concerns the review by the Federal Court of the ruling of the Court of Arbitration for Sport rejecting the complaint of an international-level athlete with differences of sex development against a non-state regulation requiring her to reduce her natural testosterone level to compete in international competitions in the female category. Having refused to undergo the treatment, she was no longer able to take part in such competitions.

001-222889.name: Ukraine and the Netherlands v. Russia
001-222889.subject: The four inter-State applications (nos. 8019/16, 43800/14, 28525/20 and 11055/22) arose from events which began in the spring of 2014 with the occupation and annexation by Russia of Crimea, part of Ukrainian sovereign territory, and the appearance of pro-Russian separatist armed groups in eastern Ukraine who subsequently took control of territory in the Donetsk and Luhansk regions and declared independence from Ukraine. The first three applications (nos. 8019/16, 43800/14 and 28525/20) concerned complaints related to the conflict in eastern Ukraine involving the separatists from spring 2014. In its two first applications (nos. 8019/16, 43800/14), the Ukrainian Government pleaded an administrative practice by Russia of numerous Convention violations. The third application (no. 28525/20), lodged by the Dutch Government, concerned alleged violations of Articles 2, 3 and 13 resulting from the downing of flight MH17. The fourth application (no. 11055/22) was joined by the Grand Chamber to the pending case on 17 February 2023 and concerned the Ukraine Government’s complaints of further administrative practices committed by the Russian Federation following its full-scale invasion beginning on 24 February 2022.
conclusions: Article 2 (substantive and procedural) (Downing of flight MH17): violations
Articles 2 and 3 (substantive), 8 and 1 of Protocol No. 1 (Military attacks): violations
Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 + Article 8: violations
Article 14 (+ 2, 3, 4 § 2, 5, 8, 9, 10 and 11 and 1 and 2 of Protocol No. 1): violation
Article 13 (+ 2, 3, 4 § 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 14 and 1 and 2 of Protocol No. 1): violation

001-243130.name: Mansouri v. Italy
001-243130.subject: The case concerned the confinement of a Tunisian national and the conditions of his seven-day return voyage to Tunis on board an Italian cruise ship following a refusal-of-entry order issued by the Italian border police as well as the domestic remedies available under Italian law.
conclusions: Article 1: Jurisdiction and responsibility of the respondent State
Article 5 §§ 1, 2 and 4: Inadmissible (non-exhaustion of domestic remedies even assuming Article 5 was applicable)

001-242521.name: Ships Waste Oil Collector B.V. and Others v. the Netherlands
001-242521.subject: The case concerned the transmission, by the Public Prosecution service, of data, lawfully obtained in the context of criminal investigations through telephone tapping, to the Netherlands Competition Authority and their use by that authority in unrelated administrative investigations into the applicant companies’ involvement in price-fixing.

001-219944.name: Fabbri and Others v. San Marino
001-219944.subject: The case concerned a complaint by the victims of alleged offences participating in criminal proceedings that the investigating judge’s inaction had led to the time-barring of those offences and thus to the non-adjudication of their civil claims.
conclusions: Article 6 § 1: applicable in relation to the third applicant and inapplicable in relation to the remaining two applicants; no violation.

001-236065.name: Pindo Mulla v. Spain
001-236065.subject: The case concerned procedural safeguards in the context of the administration of medical treatment in the form of blood transfusions to a Jehovah’s Witness, during emergency surgery, despite her expressed refusal to undergo a blood transfusion of any kind.
conclusions: Article 8 read in the light of Article 9: violation

001-234982.name: Ukraine v. Russia (re Crimea)
001-234982.subject: The two inter-State applications (nos. 20958/14 and 38334/18) concerned Ukraine’s allegations of administrative practices resulting in numerous human-rights violations under the Convention by the Russian Federation mostly in Crimea beginning on 27 February 2014, the date from when they alleged that Russia exercised extraterritorial jurisdiction over Crimea. They also concerned allegations of a pattern of prosecution of Ukrainians for their political stances and/or pro-Ukrainian activity (“Ukrainian political prisoners) which had occurred predominantly in Crimea but also in other parts of Ukraine or in the Russian Federation. The Ukrainian Government alleged that these administrative practices were part of a large, interconnected campaign of political repression implemented by the respondent State aimed at stifling any political opposition and entailed systematic violations of civil rights and freedoms
conclusions: Article 14 in conjunction with Articles 8, 9, 10, 11 and Article 2 of Protocol No. 4: violation
Article 18 in conjunction with Articles 5, 6, 8, 10 and 11: violation

001-234468.name: Nealon and Hallam v. the United Kingdom
001-234468.subject: The cases concerned the rejection of the applicants’ claim for compensation for miscarriage of justice following the quashing of their convictions as “unsafe” in the light of new evidence that had emerged. Their applications were rejected for failing to meet new statutory test, introduced after the judgment in Allen v. the United Kingdom [GC], which provided for compensation for a miscarriage of justice only where a new or newly discovered fact showed beyond reasonable doubt that the person concerned had not committed the offence.

001-233174.name: Carême v. France (dec.)

001-233261.name: Duarte Agostinho and Others v. Portugal and 32 Others (dec.)

001-233206.name: Verein KlimaSeniorinnen Schweiz and Others v. Switzerland

Article 6 § 1: violation in relation to applicant association (access to court)
Article 8: inadmissible in respect of individual applicants (incompatible ratione personae)
